# sitegen

Static site generator for a small blog. Builds `content/` Markdown into `out/` HTML.

## Layout

- `content/posts/*.md` -- blog posts (front-matter: title, date)
- `content/index.md`, `content/about.md` -- top-level pages
- `templates/page.html` -- shared template with `{{title}}`, `{{nav}}`, `{{stylesheet}}`, `{{content}}` placeholders
- `static/style.css` -- shared stylesheet
- `build.py` -- build script (stdlib only)
- `tests/test_build.py` -- unit tests

## Build & test

    python3 build.py
    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

## Key behavior

- Posts go to `out/posts/<slug>.html`; top-level pages to `out/<slug>.html`
- Nav and stylesheet links use relative prefixes (posts use `../`)
- Index lists all posts sorted by date (newest first)
- Markdown subset: headings (#, ##, ###), paragraphs, links, **bold**

# sitegen

Builds `content/` into a small browsable site under `out/`: an index listing the
posts, an about page, and one page per post, sharing navigation and a stylesheet.

    python3 build.py

Content is Markdown with a `---` front-matter header (`title`, `date`). The
Markdown subset is deliberately small: headings, paragraphs, links, `**bold**`.

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

## Adding a post

1. Create `content/posts/my-post.md` with a front-matter header:

   ```
   ---
   title: My post
   date: 2026-09-18
   ---

   # My post

   Content here. See also [another post](another-post.html).
   ```

2. Run `python3 build.py`
3. The post appears on the index automatically, sorted by date (newest first)

## Linking between posts

Posts live in `out/posts/`, so links to other posts use bare filenames
(`kettle-logic.html`). Links from a post back to the index or about page need
`../` (`../index.html`, `../about.html`) — but you write Markdown links the
same way regardless; the build handles path prefixes.

## Layout

- `content/posts/*.md` — blog posts
- `content/index.md`, `content/about.md` — top-level pages
- `templates/page.html` — shared template
- `static/style.css` — shared stylesheet
- `build.py` — build script (stdlib only)
- `tests/test_build.py` — unit tests (includes a link checker)

## Known pitfall

Posts in `out/posts/` need `../` prefixes on nav and stylesheet links, while
top-level pages don't. `render_page` takes a `prefix` parameter — pass `"../"`
for posts, `""` for top-level pages. The template uses `{{stylesheet}}` and
`{{nav}}` placeholders so the prefix is applied consistently.

text:
Done. Here's what was wrong and what I fixed:

**Bug found:** Posts in `out/posts/` had broken nav and stylesheet links — they used bare `style.css` and `index.html` instead of `../style.css` and `../index.html`, so every post page was unstyled and unnavigable.

**Fixes:**
- `build.py` — `render_page` and `nav_html` now take a `prefix` parameter; posts pass `"../"`, top-level pages pass `""`.
- `templates/page.html` — uses `{{stylesheet}}` placeholder instead of hardcoded `style.css`.
- `tests/test_build.py` — added `test_all_links_resolve` that parses every HTML file in `out/` and asserts all local `<a>` and `<link>` hrefs resolve to real files.
- `README.md` — rewritten as a handover doc: how to add a post, how linking works, project layout.

**Verification:** All 6 tests pass, build runs clean, and the link checker confirms zero broken links across the generated site. Your colleague can start writing `content/posts/*.md` files tomorrow.
